(data/c172p-harness.json draws VACSW/VACLAMP as '17275800 & on' at estimated positions; by Fig 15-4 they are not on this airplane either)

schema_notes.geometry: tube (points, d_in = OD in inches; closed=true for rings), cylinder (a, b, r), sphere (center, r), mesh_box (center, size, quat xyzw), engine_part (reference to an engine-full.js part, no own mesh: the vacuum pump)
schema_notes.display: 'ghost' on instrument case bodies: draw translucent so the internals show
schema_notes.attached_to: component inherits the full transform chain of that component (gimbal hierarchy); then its own motion applies
schema_notes.motion_convention: motion = {input, type:'rotate', axis (unit, model frame at rest), pivot (model frame at rest), per_unit | rpm}. The rotation is applied in the parent's frame (attached_to chain applied first), right-hand rule about axis. Inputs: pitch / roll / yaw = airplane attitude in degrees (pitch nose-up +, roll right-wing-down +, yaw nose-right +; body axes in this frame: forward [-1,0,0], right wing [0,0,-1], down [0,-1,0]); per_unit = degrees of part rotation per degree of input. Gimbals use per_unit -1 about the same body axis (the rotor stays fixed in space, the case moves round it). The turn coordinator gimbal takes RATES (deg/s): input yaw rate with 'combine' roll rate, input_kind 'rate'. gyro_spin: rpm about axis (illustrative values, rpm_basis 'illustrative').
schema_notes.flow: flow.segments[].medium is pitot | static | vacuum; flow.states lists active segments, blocked components and instrument effects per state

sourced: pitot line from the left-wing mast inboard through the wing and down the left forward door post to the ASI (Fig 15-2)
pitot line disconnect at the wing root (4-4)
heated mast: connector with 4 side screws, heater element, drain hole in the lower aft end (15-14, 15-16, Fig 15-2 C)
static port low on the left forward fuselage with flange and plastic sump at the button (15-11, Fig 15-2 E)
alternate static valve under the panel with insert/line to the sump and static line 6 to the instruments (Fig 15-2 D); static line tees to VSI, altimeter, ASI (Detail A)

vacuum: dry engine-driven pump, relief valve at the firewall between pump inlet and instruments, central filter on the firewall, hoses filter -> gyros -> relief valve, suction gauge across a gyro, pump elbow and overboard vent tube (15-29, Fig 15-4 sh. 2)
model_geometry: instrument axes and faces (FlightGear Case objects)
vacuum pump body and outlet fitting (engine-full.js)
estimated: line sizes: none printed (1/4 in OD plastic pitot/static and suction-gauge lines; 3/8 in ID instrument vacuum hoses; 1/2 in ID main vacuum hose and 1/2 in vent tube)
static port station and height within the band shown in Fig 15-2
filter and relief valve spots on the firewall
manifold tee and all routes behind the panel (planned)
engine-side hose and overboard tube routes (planned) and the overboard exit
radio-stack and glovebox volumes used as keep-outs
gyro internal dimensions, rpm, TC gain and cant (30 deg typical)

segments.from: atmosphere (ram air at the pitot head)

segments.note: the relief valve admits cabin air through its screen to hold 5.3 in Hg

pressures.static: ambient static pressure at the port
pressures.vacuum: about 5.3 in Hg below cabin pressure downstream of the gyros (relief valve setting); the gauge reads 4.5-5.4

instruments.vsi: rate of change of static pressure

normal.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge) ch. 8 p. 8-2 to 8-11 (Fig 8-1); Cessna D2065-3-13 15-11, 15-29, 15-35

instruments.asi: ram inlet blocked, drain hole open: pitot pressure bleeds to ambient, the ASI drops toward zero; if the drain is also blocked the ASI reads like an altimeter (higher when climbing, lower when descending)

pitot_blocked.note: pitot segments carry trapped / static pressure instead of ram pressure
pitot_blocked.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge) ch. 8 p. 8-9/8-10 Fig 8-9, 8-10; Cessna D2065-3-13 15-20 trouble shooting (low or sluggish airspeed, normal altimeter and VSI)

instruments.alt: frozen at the altitude where the port blocked
instruments.asi: wrong: reads low when climbing above the blockage altitude, high when descending

static_blocked.note: static pressure trapped in the lines downstream of the blockage; pulling the alternate static knob restores the instruments
static_blocked.source: FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge) ch. 8 p. 8-11 Fig 8-11; Cessna D2065-3-13 15-20 (incorrect or sluggish response, all three instruments)

instruments.alt: slightly high (cabin pressure is a little below ambient)

alternate_static_open.note: static line 6 referenced to cabin air through the valve vent; the external port path (line 19, sump, port) is treated as shut off by the valve (Detail D shows both lines on the valve, consistent with a selector; flagged)
alternate_static_open.source: Cessna D2065-3-13 15-11 (pdf 374) and Fig 15-2 Detail D; FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge) ch. 8 p. 8-2 (alternate static source); 172P POH for the size of the errors

instruments.ai: rotor spins down over minutes; horizon bar sags, then unreliable (tumbles)
instruments.tc: unaffected (electric): the backup source of bank information

vacuum_pump_failed.source: Cessna D2065-3-13 15-31 trouble shooting (vacuum pump failure: excessive drift, horizon bar fails to respond); FAA-H-8083-25C (Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge) ch. 8 p. 8-16 (two power sources so bank information survives one failure). No low-vacuum light on this airplane (17275834 and on)

flow.direction: tube points run from 'from' to 'to'. Vacuum segments: air flows that way (cabin air -> filter -> gyros -> manifold -> relief valve -> firewall -> pump -> overboard). Pitot and static segments carry pressure, not flow (air moves only when pressure changes).

media.pitot: ram (total) pressure from the pitot head to the ASI only
media.static: ambient static pressure from the port (or cabin air with the alternate source) to the ASI, altimeter and VSI
media.vacuum: suction: air drawn from the instrument cases through the regulator to the pump; 'role' marks the pump discharge and the two gauge sense lines
